data.text/markdown:
WECC county net load calibrated to EIA-930 balancing authority load

This marimo notebook calibrates the hourly WECC county net loads to the monthly minimum and maximum demand that each US WECC balancing authority (BA) reported to EIA Form 930, using loads.calibrate.CalibratePeaks, and combines the calibrated county net loads into a single table for review.
  • County net load. elec_net_MW = elec_total_MW - |elec_dg_MW|, from the gross county load in loads/wecc/wecc_estimate.csv.gz and the EIA-scaled rooftop PV in loads/wecc/county_dg_scaled.csv.gz. A BA's reported demand is net of behind-the-meter DG, so the net load is the calibration basis and the DG itself is held fixed.
  • BA participation. Each county's net load is split among the BAs that serve it with the factors in loads/wecc/county_ba.csv (loads/wecc/county_ba.py, fitted to EIA-861 2018 utility sales and service territories, with documented overrides in loads/wecc/county_ba_overrides.csv).
  • Targets. loads/_test/data/ba_minmax_target.csv: the monthly maximum and minimum of each BA's cleaned EIA-930 hourly demand, by UTC month.
  • Calibration. For the selected month, each BA's county shares are calibrated separately so that the peak percentile of the BA total equals the BA's reported maximum and the trough percentile equals its reported minimum. Each county's calibrated net load is the sum of its calibrated BA shares; shares in BAs without EIA-930 demand (e.g., SWPP) are left uncalibrated.
Pick the year and month, then WECC, a state, or a BA, and optionally one county of that state or BA.
